purpose: Convert the ten Phase-C survivors into durable semantic regression protection by adding independent scientific invariants to the frozen Phase-C semantic gate command, then measure by replay whether each named corruption is now detected by a matching semantic diagnostic rather than by hash or byte identity.
reviewAgent: Codex, independent reviewer and phase gatekeeper

claimBoundary.whatThisMeasures: Whether the declared semantic gate command detects twenty-two named, deliberately constructed corruptions of ten named properties, plus two adverse-record laundering attacks.
claimBoundary.whatThisDoesNotMeasure: General or future robustness of the test suite. These corruptions were authored with full knowledge of the production source and of the Phase-C battery. Detection here is TARGET COVERAGE, not evidence of detection capability against novel, unseen defects.
claimBoundary.notBlind: Unlike PHASE-C-BLIND-MUTATION-CODEX-V1, this battery is deliberately NOT blind. The ten exact corruptions are the published Phase-C survivors and the ten alternate corruptions were authored against the same known properties. The prediction is therefore LOW RISK by construction and its confirmation carries correspondingly low evidential weight about unknown defects.
priorKnowledgeAtFreeze: The full text of audits/phase-c/blind-mutation-protocol.codex.v1.json, including all ten exact patches and their frozen semanticFailurePatterns.
The full text of the four production mutation targets.
Numerical behaviour of lib/source-first-passage.js and the periodic-lattice model under corruption, measured during design at the library level (NOT through the D1 gate suite).
Clean-code expected values for every positive fixture, measured during design against unmutated production code.
No run of the frozen D1 gate suite against any mutated clone was performed before this protocol was committed.
claimBoundary.parityLadderEffect: D1 can move only P0 (computational integrity) and P1 (equation/implementation parity) evidence. It cannot move P2 or above. It produces no new observation and no new biological claim.

baseCommitPolicy.rule: The replay base commit is the D1 IMPLEMENTATION commit, which does not exist when this protocol is committed and is therefore supplied at execution time via --base-commit and recorded verbatim in the result.
runnerMustVerify: The supplied base commit is a real commit object.
The D1 PREDICTION commit that first introduced this protocol file is a STRICT ANCESTOR of the supplied base commit.

Every mutation target file at the supplied base commit hashes to the preMutationSha256 frozen below. This proves the implementation commit changed NO production mutation target and NO Phase-C evidence file.
audits/phase-d/d1-semantic-remediation-result.v1.json does not yet exist anywhere in the working tree.

measurementBoundary.measuredGate: The Phase-C semantic gate command, unchanged in form, after D1 test files are added to tests/semantic/.
measurementBoundary.classifyingCommandsOnly: Only gateCommands classify a mutation. baselineCommands are a declared SECONDARY, NON-CLASSIFYING measurement used solely to establish coverage provenance.
measurementBoundary.coverageProvenanceQuestion: For each corruption, was it ALREADY detected before D1 by a command outside the semantic gate (the ordinary test suite or an independent checker script)? This distinguishes GENUINELY NEW COVERAGE from SUITE MEMBERSHIP MIGRATION. This question is declared here, before measurement, precisely so the answer cannot be selected after the fact.
measurementBoundary.regenerationMeaning: A regeneration command propagates a production-code corruption into its generated scientific artifacts. Regeneration failure is NOT_RUN and is NOT treated as gate detection.
measurementBoundary.noGeneralizedCoverageClaim: These twenty-two probes are purposefully selected failure modes, not a representative sample of possible future defects.

classificationRules.DETECTED_SEMANTIC: The gate command exits nonzero AND at least one failure diagnostic matches a prospectively frozen semanticFailurePatterns expression naming the corrupted biological, statistical, or provenance property.
classificationRules.DETECTED_BY_HASH_ONLY: The gate command exits nonzero, no frozen semantic pattern matches, and every nonempty failure diagnostic is limited to hashes, bytes, snapshots, run IDs, or generic artifact identity.
classificationRules.SURVIVED: Every declared gate command exits zero after the exact patch is applied and every required regeneration command exits zero.
classificationRules.NOT_RUN: The clone, base verification, digest verification, exact patch, or required regeneration cannot complete, so the mutation does not reach the intended behavior.
classificationRules.INCONCLUSIVE: A gate command exits nonzero without a frozen semantic match and with diagnostics not limited to hash-only failures.
classificationRules.frozenDiagnosticMethod: Passing TAP lines beginning with a check mark or info mark are removed before semantic and hash-only pattern matching. All other stdout and stderr remain available in full logs.
classificationRules.attributionRequirement: The result MUST additionally record the exact failing test names extracted from the gate output, so that a reviewer can confirm the matched semantic pattern was produced by the INTENDED gate and not incidentally by an unrelated failing test. A mutation whose only pattern match comes from an unintended test is recorded with attributionSatisfied=false and is NOT counted toward the acceptance criterion.

toleranceRationale.principle: Every tolerance was fixed from (a) the floating-point agreement observed on UNMUTATED production code during design and (b) the analytically derived corruption magnitude. No tolerance may be changed after any mutated replay is observed.
toleranceRationale.separationMargin: Each tolerance is at least 1000x the measured clean-code noise and at least 5 orders of magnitude below the analytically derived corruption signal.

properties.title: Seconds-scale predictive density carries the change-of-variables Jacobian
properties.scientificStatement: Held-out log predictive scores are reported in nats per event on the SECONDS scale. Because the model is fitted on duration normalized by a per-state training mean (y = t / scale), the reported score must be log p_T(t) = log p_Y(y) - log(scale). Omitting -log(scale) reports a density on normalized duration while labelling it a seconds-scale density, which is dimensionally false and breaks comparability across states with different duration scales.
properties.positiveFixture: Synthetic fixture, state 2. TRAIN uncensored = 4 motors x (1,3,5,1,3,5) s = 24 dwells, sum 72 s, training mean scale = 3 s EXACTLY. HOLDOUT uncensored = 5 motors x (1,2,3,4,5) s = 25 dwells, holdout mean 3 s EXACTLY. For the memoryless model logDensity(y) = -y, so the mean held-out log score = -(3/3) - ln(3) = -1 - ln(3) = -2.0986122886681096. Measured on clean code: identical to 0 absolute error.
properties.negativeFixture: With the Jacobian omitted the same quantity is exactly -1. Separation = ln(3) = 1.0986122886681096.
properties.secondInvariant: Unit reparameterization equivariance. Re-expressing every duration in units of half-seconds (multiply all train and holdout durations by k = 2) leaves y unchanged but must shift the mean seconds-scale log score by exactly -ln(k). Measured on clean code: shift = -0.693147180559945 against -ln(2) = -0.6931471805599453, absolute error 3.3e-16. With the Jacobian omitted the shift is exactly 0.
properties.oracleIndependence: The expected values -1-ln(3) and -ln(2) are closed-form arithmetic over the fixture durations. The oracle never calls scoreEvents, logDensity, or any density routine; scoreEvents is module-private and unreachable from the test.
properties.notSatisfiedByHash: The assertion compares a numeric mean log score against a closed-form constant. It reads no sha256, no runId, no committed report file and no snapshot.

properties.title: The slow-state posterior conditions on survival, not on an instantaneous event density
properties.scientificStatement: posteriorSlowGivenSurvival(t) is the posterior probability of the slow latent component GIVEN the observation T > t. It must therefore weight components by SURVIVOR MASS w_i exp(-lambda_i t), not by EVENT DENSITY w_i lambda_i exp(-lambda_i t). These are different observations and yield different latent-state probabilities whenever the component rates differ.
properties.positiveFixture: mixture = {weightFast: 0.25, rateFast: 4, rateSlow: 0.5}. At t = 0 the survival-conditioned posterior must equal the prior slow weight exactly: 1 - weightFast = 0.75. Measured on clean code: bitwise === 0.75.
properties.negativeFixture: Under event-density conditioning the same quantity is (0.75*0.5)/(0.75*0.5 + 0.25*4) = 0.2727272727272727. Separation = 0.4772727272727273.
properties.secondInvariant: For t in {0.5, 1, 2} the returned value must equal the independently computed survivor ratio 0.75 e^{-0.5t} / (0.75 e^{-0.5t} + 0.25 e^{-4t}). Measured on clean code: absolute error 0 at all three times. This second invariant is required because a corruption that replaces rateSlow with rateFast inside the SURVIVAL form is invisible at t = 0 (both exponentials equal 1) and is caught only at t > 0.
properties.oracleIndependence: The oracle recomputes the declared survivor ratio inline from Math.exp and the literal mixture constants. It does not call posteriorSlowGivenSurvival to build its own expectation.
properties.notSatisfiedByHash: The assertion is a numeric comparison against closed-form exponentials with no artifact, hash, or snapshot involvement.
properties.knownGap: The pre-existing H3 check asserts only MONOTONICITY of the posterior curve. Both the correct survivor form and the event-density form are monotone increasing here, which is why monotonicity alone did not detect CXM02.

properties.title: Dispersion estimates use the n-1 sample-variance denominator
properties.scientificStatement: Quantities reported as SAMPLE variance, squared coefficient of variation, and PIT variance must use the unbiased n-1 denominator. Using the population denominator n systematically shrinks every finite-sample dispersion estimate by the factor (n-1)/n while continuing to report it as a sample estimate, which understates overdispersion and misreports calibration.
properties.positiveFixture: sampleVariance([2,4,4,4,5,5,7,9]) with mean 5 and summed squared deviation 32 over n = 8 must equal 32/7 = 4.571428571428571. Measured on clean code: bitwise === 32/7. Also sampleVariance([1,3]) = 2, and sampleVariance([5]) = 0 by the declared n < 2 rule.
properties.negativeFixture: The population denominator gives 32/8 = 4 and 2/2 = 1. Separation on the primary fixture = 0.571428571428571.
properties.secondInvariant: Report-level propagation, structurally independent of the exported function. For the same synthetic fixture the held-out state summary reports cvSquared = sampleVariance(durations)/mean^2. Holdout durations are five copies of (1,2,3,4,5) so mean = 3 and summed squared deviation = 50 over n = 25, giving cvSquared = (50/24)/9 = 0.2314814814814815 EXACTLY. Under the population denominator it is (50/25)/9 = 0.2222222222222222. Measured on clean code: absolute error 0. This catches a corruption that bypasses the exported helper.
properties.oracleIndependence: Both expectations are closed-form rationals computed by hand from literal fixture values. The oracle does not call sampleVariance to form its own expectation.
properties.notSatisfiedByHash: Both assertions compare numbers against literal rationals.

properties.title: The observation record excludes hidden world truth and the agent never receives the world object
properties.scientificStatement: observeWorld implements the declared Markov boundary. Latent world variables that no physical instrument measures (true gradient, methylation, CheY-P, position, torque, stator occupancy, CW bias, rotor angle, previous ligand) must not cross it. If they do, an observation record contains oracle truth and the claimed world/agent separation is invalid.
properties.positiveFixture: The observation key set is exactly the nine declared keys: deviceTimeMs, ligandUm, loadPnNm, motorSpeedRpm, pmfMv, receivedAtMs, receptorActivity, rotation, source. Measured on clean code: exactly these nine.
properties.negativeFixture: Any added key, e.g. trueGradient or methylationLevel, changes the key set and fails.
properties.secondInvariant: Value-level, name-independent leak detection. Two worlds are constructed that differ ONLY in hidden fields (trueGradient rising vs falling, methylation 2.2 vs 7.9, cheYpUm 3.2 vs 9.9, xUm 1 vs -50, yUm 2 vs 33, torquePnNm 700 vs 111, stators 5 vs 1, cwBias 0.25 vs 0.99, rotorAngleRad 0.4 vs 3.3, previousLigandUm 0.9 vs 0.1) and agree on every observable field. Their observation records must be deeply equal. Measured on clean code: equal. This detects a leak under ANY field name, including a renamed or numerically encoded one, and is therefore not defeated by renaming the leaked field.
properties.thirdInvariant: The agent boundary. stepAgent has arity 3 and receives an Observation, never a world. After a step, agent.lastObservation must contain no key outside the declared nine.
properties.oracleIndependence: The declared key set is a literal frozen list in the test. The two-world comparison uses createWorld and observeWorld only as the system under test; the expectation (equality) is structural and is not computed by any production function.
properties.notSatisfiedByHash: The assertions compare key sets and deep object equality, never a digest.

properties.title: Live instrument stator occupancy is clamped to the declared physical range 0..11
properties.scientificStatement: A flagellar motor cannot host negative stator units, and the declared model maximum is eleven. The live serial aperture must clamp an out-of-range instrument reading into 0..11 rather than admitting an impossible measurement into model state.
properties.positiveFixture: instrumentObservation with stators = 20 returns 11; stators = -3 returns 0; stators = 11 returns 11; stators = 0 returns 0; stators = 7 returns 7; stators absent returns null; stators = 'abc' returns null. All measured on clean code.
properties.negativeFixture: Removing the clamp returns 20 and -3 unchanged. Widening the clamp to 0..20 returns 20.
properties.oracleIndependence: Expected values are literal integers written in the test. The oracle does not call clamp or instrumentObservation to form its expectation.
properties.notSatisfiedByHash: The assertions compare returned numbers against literal integers.
properties.declaredLimitation: ADVERSE FINDING, recorded rather than fixed. Production accepts NON-INTEGRAL occupancy: instrumentObservation({stators: 7.5}) returns 7.5. The plan's minimum invariant example describes live stator occupancy as 'integral and bounded 0..11'. Integrality is NOT enforced by production and no repository document declares it. This protocol therefore gates ONLY the declared 0..11 bound and records the integrality sub-property as NOT_ESTABLISHED. Production is deliberately NOT changed to satisfy a test.

properties.title: Target stator occupancy is a declared increasing function of mechanical load
properties.scientificStatement: The synthetic world encodes mechanosensitive recruitment as statorTarget = 1 + 10 * L/(L + 420). Occupancy must therefore increase strictly with external load, approaching 1 at zero load and 11 at large load. A load-independent target erases the declared mechanosensitivity while the model continues to be described as load-responsive.
properties.positiveFixture: Agent side, exact and single-call: stepAgent predictedStators equals 1 + 10*L/(L+420) exactly at L = 0 (=1), L = 700 (=7.25), and L = 3780 (=10). World side: iterating stepWorld to steady state gives 2.9230769230769305 at L = 100 against target 2.9230769230769234 (error 7.1e-15) and 10.225092250922453 at L = 5000 against target 10.22509225092251 (error 5.7e-14).
properties.negativeFixture: A constant target of 6 gives 6 at both loads and a load difference of 0 instead of 7.302. A sign-inverted target 11 - 10*L/(L+420) gives a DECREASING relation.
properties.secondInvariant: Direction, independent of the exact functional form: steady-state occupancy at L = 5000 must exceed occupancy at L = 100 by more than 5 stator units.
properties.oracleIndependence: The expected value is the declared closed form evaluated in the test from literal load constants. The world integration is the system under test; the expectation is arithmetic.
properties.notSatisfiedByHash: The assertions compare occupancy numbers against a closed-form expression.

properties.title: First-passage mixture coefficients are a normalized Bernoulli convolution and S(0) = 1
properties.scientificStatement: sourceCoefficients builds the component weights as a convolution of independent Bernoulli(c_i) choices. The weights are a probability distribution: they are non-negative, they sum to one, and consequently the survival function at time zero equals one. If they do not, the D-L-T mixture is not a probability distribution and every integrated event probability is false.
properties.positiveFixture: With c1 = 0.3, c2 = 0.5, c3 = 0.2: N = 1 gives EXACTLY [0.7, 0.3]; N = 2 gives EXACTLY [0.35, 0.5, 0.15]; N = 3 gives [0.28, 0.47, 0.22, 0.03] within 1e-12. Sums equal 1 and sourceSurvival(0, N) equals 1 for N = 1, 2, 3. All measured on clean code.
properties.negativeFixture: Shifting mass by (1-c) instead of c gives [0.7, 0.7] at N = 1 with sum 1.4. Dropping the complement gives [0.3, 0.3] with sum 0.6.
properties.orderSensitivity: The full coefficient VECTOR is asserted, not only its sum, because a corruption that swaps the retain and shift factors still sums to one but reverses the component ordering. A sum-only gate would be vacuous against that swap.
properties.oracleIndependence: The expected vectors are computed by hand from the Bernoulli convolution and written as literals. The oracle does not call sourceCoefficients to form its expectation.
properties.notSatisfiedByHash: The assertions compare coefficient vectors and sums against literal rationals.
properties.coverageProvenanceNote: tests/science-gates.test.mjs already asserts the coefficient SUM and S(0) at 1e-12. That file is part of npm test, which the Phase-C protocol explicitly excluded from per-mutation classification. The honest D1 claim for this property is SUITE MEMBERSHIP MIGRATION plus a genuinely new order-sensitivity assertion, not new detection of a previously undetectable defect. The result must record the measured baseline outcome.

properties.title: The competing-risk off hazard carries N-fold detachment multiplicity and conserves event mass
properties.scientificStatement: With N occupied stators there are N independent baseline detachment opportunities, so the off hazard must contain stateN * sigmaMinus, not sigmaMinus. Omitting the multiplicity understates the off hazard and, because the total rate still carries it, breaks the conservation identity that total event density equals the negative derivative of survival.
properties.positiveFixture: Literal parameters kPlusByN[2] = 0.2, sigmaPlus = 1.5, sigmaMinus = 0.5, c1 = 0.3, c2 = 0.5. At N = 2 the three terms must have offRate EXACTLY [1, 2, 3] and totalRate EXACTLY [1.2, 2.2, 3.2]. Measured on clean code: exact.
properties.negativeFixture: Dropping the multiplicity gives offRate [0.5, 1.5, 2.5]. Dropping the component term gives offRate [1, 1, 1].
properties.secondInvariant: Density-survival conservation, a structurally independent numerical oracle. total(t) + dS/dt must vanish, where dS/dt is a central difference of sourceSurvival with step 1e-5. Measured on clean code at t = 1: residual 1.7e-11 at N = 2 and 1.9e-11 at N = 3. The analytic corruption residual is (N-1) * sigmaMinus * S(t) = 0.0835 at N = 2 and 0.0885 at N = 3, seven orders above tolerance.
properties.invisibilityTrap: The conservation residual is identically (N-1)*sigmaMinus*S(t), which is EXACTLY ZERO at N = 1. A gate fixtured only at N = 1 is vacuous against this corruption. This protocol therefore asserts conservation at N = 2 and N = 3.
properties.oracleIndependence: The offRate expectations are literal arithmetic. The conservation oracle differentiates sourceSurvival numerically, which is a different function from sourceTerms and sourceDensities under test, and the identity itself is derived from the model definition rather than from any production routine.
properties.notSatisfiedByHash: Both assertions compare rates and residuals against literal numbers.
properties.coverageProvenanceNote: tests/science-gates.test.mjs already asserts density = -dS/dt at 2e-8 over states 1..8. As with D1P07 this lives in npm test, excluded from Phase-C classification. The honest D1 claim is SUITE MEMBERSHIP MIGRATION plus a new explicit offRate multiplicity fixture. The result must record the measured baseline outcome.

properties.title: The exponential-mixture second moment retains its factor of two
properties.scientificStatement: For a mixture of exponentials E[T^2] = 2 * sum_i w_i / R_i^2. Dropping the factor of two halves every second moment and reports a memoryless exponential, whose squared coefficient of variation is exactly one, as though it had zero normalized variance.
properties.positiveFixture: Literal single-exponential parameters kPlusByN[0] = 0.25 with stateN = 0 and codeN0Branch = false, which yields exactly one term with totalRate 0.25 and offRate 0. Then meanDwellSeconds = 4 and normalizedVariance = 1. Measured on clean code: bitwise exact at both.
properties.negativeFixture: Without the factor of two normalizedVariance is exactly 0. Separation = 1. With a factor of three it is 2.
properties.secondInvariant: Quadrature oracle on a multi-component state, structurally independent of the moment routine. E[T^2] = integral of 2 t S(t) dt. At N = 2 with the D1P08 literal parameters the analytic second moment is 0.722019556359045 and Simpson quadrature of 2 t sourceSurvival(t) gives 0.7220195563588557, relative error 2.6e-13.
properties.oracleIndependence: The single-exponential expectation E[T^2] = 2/rate^2 and CV^2 = 1 are textbook closed forms written as literals. The quadrature oracle integrates sourceSurvival, a different function from sourceMoments under test.
properties.notSatisfiedByHash: The assertions compare moments against closed-form constants and a numerical integral.
properties.coverageProvenanceNote: normalizedVariance has NO reader anywhere in the JavaScript codebase outside its own definition. Neither npm test nor any independent checker asserts it. This property is expected to be the one case of GENUINELY NEW COVERAGE among D1P07, D1P08 and D1P09. The result must record the measured baseline outcome.

properties.title: The finite occupancy lattice is a periodic 13-site ring including the wraparound bond
properties.scientificStatement: The exact occupancy model is a 13-site periodic lattice gas whose adjacency counts all thirteen nearest-neighbour bonds, including the bond joining site 13 to site 1. Replacing the ring by an open chain silently deletes one of thirteen bonds, changing the partition function, the fitted cooperativity J, and the structural interpretation, while the model continues to be described as a periodic motor ring.
properties.positiveFixture: An independent Node reimplementation enumerates all 2^13 = 8192 states with explicit modulo-13 wraparound, forms the Boltzmann distribution exp(J*adjacent + mu*count), marginalizes to occupancy 0..13, and recomputes the sum of squared residuals against the source-pinned Franco-Onate 2025 occupancy distributions at the artifact's OWN reported J and muByBead. Measured on clean code: recomputed SSE 0.049767727747922194 against reported 0.04976772774792293, absolute error 7.4e-16.
properties.negativeFixture: The same recomputation under open-chain adjacency gives 0.05002749563050486, an absolute deviation of 2.6e-4 from the reported value, which is 2.6e6 times the declared tolerance.
properties.secondInvariant: Anti-vacuity discrimination control. The test additionally asserts that the periodic and open-chain recomputations at the reported parameters DIFFER by more than 1e-6. This proves the gate is genuinely sensitive to the wraparound bond rather than passing for an unrelated reason, and it also fires if a corruption drives the fitted J toward zero, where the two topologies coincide and the primary check would lose power.
properties.thirdInvariant: Hand-calculable adjacency fixtures on the oracle's own lattice: the configuration with only sites 1 and 13 occupied has periodic adjacency 1 and open-chain adjacency 0; the fully occupied ring has adjacency 13 versus 12; the alternating configuration has adjacency 0 under both.
properties.oracleIndependence: The oracle is a pure JavaScript reimplementation of the declared statistical-mechanics model. It does not execute, import, or parse scripts/run-cross-study-parity.py. It consumes only the source-pinned observed distributions and the artifact's own reported parameters, and it recomputes the goodness-of-fit itself.
properties.notSatisfiedByHash: The gate compares recomputed floating-point physics against reported floating-point physics. The audit artifact's recorded sha256 of the Python runner is explicitly NOT used, because a regenerating mutant rewrites that digest with its own value and the check would degrade to hash identity.
properties.coverageProvenanceNote: scripts/independent-cross-study-check.mjs already performs an equivalent periodic recomputation at 1e-10. It runs under npm run cross-study:verify, a command outside the Phase-C semantic gate. The honest D1 claim for this property is SUITE MEMBERSHIP MIGRATION plus a new anti-vacuity discrimination control. The result must record the measured baseline outcome.
properties.declaredLimitation: The anti-vacuity control couples topology correctness to the fitted J being identifiably nonzero. A future honest refit yielding J near zero would fail this control for a scientific rather than a corruption reason. This coupling is declared here rather than discovered later.

properties.title: The historical Phase-C 0/10 adverse result remains present, unlaundered, and internally consistent
properties.scientificStatement: The Phase-C blind battery produced 10 SURVIVED and 0 DETECTED_SEMANTIC. That is adverse evidence about semantic coverage and it must remain visible with the same prominence as any favourable later result. Deleting it, editing its counts, relabelling an outcome, or silently diverging the canonical result from its preserved evidence copy is truth laundering.
properties.positiveFixture: audits/phase-c/blind-mutation-result.codex.v1.json exists; classificationCounts equals exactly {DETECTED_SEMANTIC: 0, DETECTED_BY_HASH_ONLY: 0, SURVIVED: 10, NOT_RUN: 0, INCONCLUSIVE: 0}; all ten CXM ids are present; every outcome classification is SURVIVED; and the preserved evidence copy at audits/phase-c/blind-mutation-evidence.codex.v1/blind-mutation-result.codex.v1.json is byte-identical to the canonical file (both sha256 e36bdfb01fd51a4acb078762da1edff9deef4ff0844cf8f80d00c68d400be7d1).
properties.negativeFixture: Any count edit, any relabelled outcome, a missing file, or divergence between the canonical file and its evidence copy fails with a diagnostic naming the adverse Phase-C record.
properties.oracleIndependence: The expected counts and ids are literal constants frozen in the test and independently restated in this protocol. The check does not consult the Phase-C runner or its classifier.
properties.notSatisfiedByHash: The primary assertions are on parsed COUNTS and ids, which are semantic content. The canonical-versus-evidence byte comparison is an additional consistency assertion, not the basis of the gate; the count and id assertions fail on their own under laundering.

executionProtocol.cloneStrategy: One git clone --no-local --no-checkout per mutation, configured core.autocrlf=false and detached at the supplied base commit before patching. No dependency install is performed; every declared command runs on Node builtins, repository sources, and the system Python.
executionProtocol.primaryCheckoutPolicy: The runner records primary HEAD and porcelain status before and after execution, writes only beneath the explicit scratch root, and fails its final status if the primary checkout changes.
executionProtocol.scratchSafety: Execution requires an absolute, absent-or-empty scratch root outside the primary checkout.
executionProtocol.targetVerification: SHA-256 is computed over raw target bytes before UTF-8 patching. The exact before text must occur once and the exact after text must not already exist.
executionProtocol.logging: Every command receives separate lossless UTF-8 stdout and stderr files with exit code, signal, byte count, and SHA-256.
executionProtocol.phaseCPreservationCheck: Before any clone, the runner verifies that every file under audits/phase-c/ in the primary checkout hashes to its value recorded in audits/phase-d/phase-c-preservation-baseline.v1.json, and refuses to execute otherwise.

acceptanceCriteria.AC4: attributionSatisfied is true for all twenty-two: the matched pattern is produced by the intended gate test.
acceptanceCriteria.AC5: At least one alternate-form corruption per property is detected. Ten alternates cover the ten properties.
acceptanceCriteria.AC6: Both adverse-record laundering attacks are detected.
acceptanceCriteria.AC7: The original Phase-C evidence remains byte-identical across the whole phase.
acceptanceCriteria.AC8: Clean-tree focused tests and the required validation baseline pass, except cross-study:verify-raw which is BLOCKED_EXTERNAL and npm audit development-dependency findings which are reported separately.

acceptanceCriteria.AC10: The coverage-provenance table honestly separates genuinely new coverage from suite-membership migration for every property.
